lastText: File ClosedThe Alliance That HeldMajor VictoryThe War Cabinet and Chiefs of Staff, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign ███████ its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's ███████ forks. Market Garden's reach for Arnhem was scaled back before it happened rather than mourned after: Browning's private reservation taken seriously instead of overruled. The February 1945 eastern-city raids were declined: Dresden never becomes the word it became, and the oil and rail campaigns finished the war's arithmetic without it, exactly as their own advocates' logic implied they could. Coalition Cohesion held solid across the war's hardest disagreements: the Western partnership that █████ anchor NATO within a few years was, on this path, unusually strong from the very start.
